title: Protocol to Calculate Aircraft Emissions for International Air Routes in South America
author: Cui, Lei, et al.
materials: Generally, the primary calculation methods for non-CO2 emissions are the ICAO method (Boeing Fuel Flow Method 2 (BFFM2) method and First Order Approximation (FOA) method.19,24 Therefore, this protocol proposes a Modified BFFM2-FOA-FPM method based on the Fuel Percentage Method (FPM). This method combines the BFFM2-FOA method and the Fuel Percentage Method (FPM),25 which can calculate the CO2 and non-CO2 emissions simultaneously. Some papers have focused on calculating CO2 and non-CO2 emissions, but no unified approach exists to connect the two accounting methods. Furthermore, the calculation method of CO2 emissions has not considered the difference of sub-series, and that of non-CO2 emissions has not focused on the emissions in the CCD stage. Therefore, we built a new Modified BFFM2-FOA-FPM method to calculate CO2 and non-CO2 emissions from the CCD stage. The LTO emissions are calculated using the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). And our approach has considered the aircraft types' emission intensity. We divide the route distance into several groups and get the six pollutions of aircraft types in these different distances to ensure that the calculation results are accurate. Compared with existing research, our results cover more detailed aircraft types, and we corrected the results with the actual flight time to make it more real. In addition, our method can calculate the PM2.5 of the CCD stage. Existing studies focus on calculating PM2.5 in the LTO stage, while there are few corresponding calculation methods for PM2.5 in the CCD stage. The Modified BFFM2-FOA-FPM method can estimate the PM2.5 value of the CCD stage.

steps.title: Download ICAO Emissions Databank
steps.instruction: Log on to https://www.easa.europa.eu/domains/environment/icao-aircraft-engine-emissions-databank and download the latest ICAO Aircraft Engine Emissions Databank, which contains emission data for six pollutants for all engine types in an LTO cycle.

steps.title: Build Engine Database per Aircraft
steps.instruction: Using the flight information collected earlier, create a database that lists for each aircraft its type, engine type(s) and number of engines; this will link each aircraft to the corresponding entries in the ICAO emissions databank.

substeps.instruction: Note: The study assumes standard aviation kerosene (Jet‑A); relevant fuel data are available via the KRT link (Downloads‑Emissions Databank (07/2021)‑Gaseous Emissions and Smoke).
Example: For the Medellín‑Caracas route in 2019, the aircraft type is 737‑400, engine type CFM56‑3B2, with two engines.

steps.title: Obtain Standard LTO Emissions
steps.instruction: Extract from the ICAO databank the standard LTO‑cycle emissions for each aircraft‑engine combination; record CO₂ (tons), HC (g), CO (g), NOₓ (g), PM₂.₅ (g) and SO₂ (g).

substeps.instruction: Example for a 737‑400 (2 CFM56‑3B2 engines): CO₂ = 2.658194 t, HC = 674.830 g, CO = 11976.422 g, NOₓ = 8425.296 g, PM₂.₅ = 170.640 g, SO₂ = 3258.54 g per LTO cycle.

steps.title: Calculate Total LTO Emissions
steps.instruction: For each aircraft, multiply the standard LTO emissions by the flight frequency for the study period; if a flight is a transit (multiple take‑offs/landings), multiply by the number of LTO cycles (2 for two take‑offs, 3 for three, etc.). Sum across all aircraft to obtain total LTO emissions for the region.

substeps.instruction: Example (Avior Airlines, Medellín‑Caracas 2019): total LTO emissions = 1658.713 t CO₂, 7.473288 t CO, 0.421094 t HC, 5.257385 t NOₓ, 0.10648 t PM₂.₅, 2.033329 t SO₂.

steps.title: Determine CCD Emission Intensities
steps.instruction: Compute emission intensities for the cruise‑climb‑descent (CCD) stage using the Modified BFFM2‑FOA‑FPM method.

substeps.instruction: b. For each aircraft and each segment, calculate the unknown ratio ratiocr by integrating fuel volume per unit flying time (from aircraft performance data) with the ICAO emission coefficients, then correct ratiocr using the actual flight time collected for the segment.
c. Obtain CO₂ emission intensity (kg fuel × CO₂‑per‑kg‑fuel) for each aircraft‑segment pair using the determined ratiocr; this intensity is later used for both CO₂ and the other five pollutants.
d. Compute emission intensities for the remaining pollutants:

• CO and HC intensities: Ij = Ij₀ × θ³·³ × δ¹·⁰², where Ij₀ is the LTO‑stage standard coefficient (g kg⁻¹), θ = T_outside/288 K, δ = P_external/sea‑level P. Interpolate θ and δ for cruising altitude (assumed 10 000 m) using temperature‑altitude and pressure‑altitude relationships.

• NOₓ intensity: INOx = Ij₀ × δ⁰·⁵¹ × θ¹·⁶⁵ × exp[19.0 × (0.0063 − 0.622 × φ × Pv / P − φ × Pv)], where φ is relative humidity, Pv is saturation pressure; obtain θ, δ, φ, P, Pv by interpolation at the cruise altitude.

• PM₂.₅ intensity is derived by separating Non‑volatile Component Fine Particles (NCFP) and Volatile Component Fine Particles (VCFP) using the Modified BFFM2‑FOA‑FPM calculations (no explicit formula given).

e. Compile a data sheet listing the six‑pollutant emission intensities for every aircraft type in each distance segment. Note: this sheet is specific to the studied region; for a new region the entire procedure must be repeated.

steps.title: Compute CCD Emissions
steps.instruction: For each aircraft, multiply the CCD emission intensity (from step 5) by the actual flight distance, flight frequency, and the number of take‑offs/landings for transit flights; sum across all aircraft to obtain total CCD emissions.

substeps.instruction: If a flight is a transit with two take‑offs/landings, use the sum of the two segment distances; if three segments are involved, sum the three distances before multiplication.

steps.title: Finalize and Document Results
steps.instruction: Aggregate LTO and CCD emissions to obtain overall emissions for the study area; record the methodology, assumptions (e.g., 10 000 m cruise altitude, standard Jet‑A fuel), timing (LTO = 4 days, CCD = 10 days), and computational resources (Intel Core i7‑8550U, 16 GB RAM, 64‑bit Windows 10). Include accuracy analysis comparing calculated totals (e.g., 5 867 289.72 t CO₂) with reference estimates (5 375 772–5 931 887 t CO₂) and report error range (1.09 %–9.14 %, average 5.115 %).
